```
            {
                "type": "gNB",
                "global_gnb_id": {
                    "plmn": {"mcc": "001", "mnc": "03"},
                    "gnb_id": 2,
                    "bit_length": 22
                },
                "name": "gnb-west",
                "supported_tas": [
                    {
                        "tac": "000001",
                        "broadcast_plmns": [
                            {
                                "plmn": {"mcc": "001", "mnc": "03"},
                                "snssais": [{"sst": 1}]
                            }
                        ]
                    }
                ],
                "default_paging_drx": 128,
                "state": "setup_failed",
                "setup_failure": {
                    "cause": "Unknown PLMN or SNPN",
                    "reason": "no operator serves a broadcast PLMN",
                    "at": "2026-11-13T16:32:10.120934871Z"
                },
                "connected_at": "2026-11-13T16:32:10.118410254Z",
                "tnl_addresses": ["127.0.0.2"],
                "ue_connections": 0
            }
        ],
        "page": 1,
        "per_page": 25,
        "total_count": 4
    }
}
```

## Get a Radio

This path returns a radio, with its UE connections by operator. To list its UE connections, use [`GET /api/v1/ue-connections?radio={ref}`](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/reference/api/ue_connections/index.md#list-ue-connections>).

| Method | Path |
| --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/radios/{ref}` |

### Path Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ref` | string | Radio identity, as returned in a radio's `ref` field, for example `eNB:001-01:MacroeNB-0019b` or `gNB:001-01:000001@22`. See [Radio Ref](<#radio-ref>). `:` and `@` can be percent-encoded. |

### Response Fields

The fields of [List Radios](<#list-radios>), plus:

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ue_connections_by_operator` | array | UE-associated logical S1-connections or NG-connections from the radio, by operator. Lists every operator that owns a PLMN the radio broadcasts, and every other operator with UE connections from the radio, sorted by operator name. Absent when empty. |
| `ue_connections_by_operator[].operator` | string | Operator name. |
| `ue_connections_by_operator[].ue_connections` | int | UE-associated logical S1-connections or NG-connections. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "ref": "eNB:001-01:MacroeNB-0019c",
        "type": "eNB",
        "global_enb_id": {
            "plmn": {"mcc": "001", "mnc": "01"},
            "enb_id_type": "macro",
            "enb_id": 412
        },
        "name": "enb-south",
        "supported_tas": [
            {
                "tac": "000001",
                "broadcast_plmns": [
                    {"plmn": {"mcc": "001", "mnc": "01"}},
                    {"plmn": {"mcc": "001", "mnc": "02"}}
                ]
            }
        ],
        "default_paging_drx": 128,
        "state": "up",
        "connected_at": "2026-11-13T16:31:55.645045565Z",
        "tnl_addresses": ["127.0.0.1"],
        "ue_connections": 1,
        "ue_connections_by_operator": [
            {"operator": "Operator A", "ue_connections": 0},
            {"operator": "Operator B", "ue_connections": 1}
        ]
    }
}
```

# Status

## Get the Status

This path returns the version of the MOCN, whether it is initialized, and whether user-plane aggregation is enabled.

| Method | Path |
| --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/status` |

### Response Fields

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | string | Version. |
| `revision` | string | Git commit of the build. Empty in development builds. |
| `initialized` | boolean | Whether the first user exists. See [Initialize](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/reference/api/initialize/index.md>). |
| `user_plane_aggregation` | boolean | Whether operators can use user-plane aggregation: `ran.user_plane.enabled` in the configuration file. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "version": "v0.0.1",
        "revision": "",
        "initialized": true,
        "user_plane_aggregation": false
    }
}
```

## Check Liveness

This path answers while the process serves HTTP.

| Method | Path |
| --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/livez` |

It answers `204 No Content`.

## Check Readiness

This path returns whether the MOCN is ready to receive traffic. The response has `Cache-Control: no-store`.

| Method | Path |
| --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/readyz` |

### Checks

| Name | Passes when |
| --- | --- |
| `database` | The database answers. |

### Response Fields

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ready` | boolean | Whether every check passes. |
| `checks` | array | The checks, in order. |
| `checks[].name` | string | Name of the check. |
| `checks[].ok` | boolean | Whether it passes. |
| `checks[].detail` | string | Why it fails. Empty when it passes. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "ready": true,
        "checks": [
            {"name": "database", "ok": true, "detail": ""}
        ]
    }
}
```

# UE Connections

A UE connection is a UE-associated logical S1-connection or NG-connection that Ella MOCN relays between a radio and an operator's MME or AMF. UE connections are learned at runtime, not stored.

## List UE Connections

This path returns the UE connections, oldest first.

| Method | Path |
| --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/ue-connections` |

### Query Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page` | query | int | `1` | `>= 1` | 1-based page index. |
| `per_page` | query | int | `25` | `1…100` | Number of items per page. |
| `radio` | query | string |  |  | Only the UE connections of the radio with this [`ref`](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/reference/api/radios/index.md#list-radios>). |
| `operator` | query | string |  |  | Only the UE connections of the [operator](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/reference/api/operators/index.md>) with this name. |

### Response Fields

`items` holds the UE connections of the page, `page` and `per_page` echo the query, and `total_count` is the number of UE connections that match the filters. Each UE connection has:

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `interface` | string | `s1` or `ng`. |
| `radio` | object | The connection between the radio and Ella MOCN. |
| `radio.ref` | string | The radio's [`ref`](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/reference/api/radios/index.md#list-radios>). |
| `radio.enb_ue_s1ap_id` | int | S1 only. eNB UE S1AP ID, allocated by the radio. `0` to `16777215`. Absent until the radio answers a HANDOVER REQUEST. |
| `radio.mme_ue_s1ap_id` | int | S1 only. MME UE S1AP ID, allocated by Ella MOCN. `0` to `4294967295`. |
| `radio.ran_ue_ngap_id` | int | NG only. RAN UE NGAP ID, allocated by the radio. `0` to `4294967295`. Absent until the radio answers a HANDOVER REQUEST. |
| `radio.amf_ue_ngap_id` | int | NG only. AMF UE NGAP ID, allocated by Ella MOCN. `0` to `1099511627775`. |
| `mme` | object | S1 only. The S1 connection between Ella MOCN and the operator's MME. |
| `mme.tnl_addresses` | array | The MME's TNL addresses, as configured on the operator. |
| `mme.enb_ue_s1ap_id` | int | eNB UE S1AP ID, allocated by Ella MOCN. `0` to `16777215`. |
| `mme.mme_ue_s1ap_id` | int | MME UE S1AP ID, allocated by the MME. Absent until the MME's first message for the UE. |
| `amf` | object | NG only. The NG connection between Ella MOCN and the operator's AMF. |
| `amf.tnl_addresses` | array | The AMF's TNL addresses, as configured on the operator. |
| `amf.ran_ue_ngap_id` | int | RAN UE NGAP ID, allocated by Ella MOCN. `0` to `4294967295`. |
| `amf.amf_ue_ngap_id` | int | AMF UE NGAP ID, allocated by the AMF. Absent until the AMF's first message for the UE. |
| `operator` | string | Name of the operator that serves the selected PLMN. |
| `plmn` | object | The selected PLMN, with `mcc` and `mnc`. |
| `since` | string | When Ella MOCN received the INITIAL UE MESSAGE, HANDOVER REQUEST or PATH SWITCH REQUEST. |
| `tai` | object | The last TAI the radio reported for the UE: `plmn` and `tac`, 6 lower-case hexadecimal digits. Absent when none. |
| `ecgi` | object | S1 only. The last E-UTRAN CGI the radio reported for the UE: `plmn` and `cell_id`, the 28-bit E-UTRAN Cell Identity. Absent when none. |
| `nr_cgi` | object | NG only. The last NR CGI the radio reported for the UE: `plmn` and `cell_id`, the 36-bit NR Cell Identity. Absent when none. |
| `tunnels` | array | With user-plane aggregation, the GTP-U tunnels Ella MOCN relays for the UE. Absent when none. |
| `tunnels[].bearer` | int | E-RAB ID or PDU session ID. |
| `tunnels[].direction` | string | `uplink` (from the radio) or `downlink` (from the operator). |
| `tunnels[].forwarding` | boolean | Handover data forwarding tunnel. |
| `tunnels[].address`, `tunnels[].teid` | string, int | Ella MOCN's endpoint the sender uses. |
| `tunnels[].peer_address`, `tunnels[].peer_teid` | string, int | The endpoint Ella MOCN forwards to. |
| `tunnels[].packets`, `tunnels[].bytes` | int | G-PDUs relayed so far, and the octets of their T-PDUs: the inner IP packet, without the GTP-U header and extension headers. End Marker and Tunnel Status messages are not counted. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "interface": "s1",
                "radio": {
                    "ref": "eNB:001-01:MacroeNB-0019c",
                    "enb_ue_s1ap_id": 1,
                    "mme_ue_s1ap_id": 1
                },
                "mme": {
                    "tnl_addresses": ["127.0.0.3"],
                    "enb_ue_s1ap_id": 1,
                    "mme_ue_s1ap_id": 101
                },
                "operator": "Operator B",
                "plmn": {"mcc": "001", "mnc": "02"},
                "since": "2026-11-13T16:31:56.646031138Z",
                "tai": {
                    "plmn": {"mcc": "001", "mnc": "02"},
                    "tac": "000001"
                },
                "ecgi": {
                    "plmn": {"mcc": "001", "mnc": "02"},
                    "cell_id": 105473
                }
            },
            {
                "interface": "ng",
                "radio": {
                    "ref": "gNB:001-01:000001@22",
                    "ran_ue_ngap_id": 0,
                    "amf_ue_ngap_id": 2
                },
                "amf": {
                    "tnl_addresses": ["127.0.0.2"],
                    "ran_ue_ngap_id": 2,
                    "amf_ue_ngap_id": 101
                },
                "operator": "Operator A",
                "plmn": {"mcc": "001", "mnc": "01"},
                "since": "2026-11-13T16:31:56.646102232Z",
                "tai": {
                    "plmn": {"mcc": "001", "mnc": "01"},
                    "tac": "000001"
                },
                "nr_cgi": {
                    "plmn": {"mcc": "001", "mnc": "01"},
                    "cell_id": 16384
                }
            }
        ],
        "page": 1,
        "per_page": 25,
        "total_count": 2
    }
}
```

# Users

Paths under `/api/v1/users/me` act on the user of the token. The others require Admin, and an access token: an API token gets `403`.

## Get My User

| Method | Path |
| --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/users/me` |

### Response Fields

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `email` | string | Email address. |
| `role_id` | int | `1` to `3`. See [roles](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/reference/api/index.md#roles>). |
| `password_set` | boolean | The user has a password. |
| `oidc_linked` | boolean | The user is linked to an account at the current [identity provider](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/reference/api/oidc/index.md>). |

The other paths that return users return the same fields.

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "email": "admin@example.com",
        "role_id": 1,
        "password_set": true,
        "oidc_linked": false
    }
}
```

## Update My Password

This path ends the user's sessions, except the one of the session cookie the request carries. Without that cookie, it ends all of them. It requires an access token.

| Method | Path |
| --- | --- |
| PUT | `/api/v1/users/me/password` |

### Request Body

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `current_password` | string | Yes | Current password. |
| `password` | string | Yes | New password, 8 to 72 bytes. |

### Sample Request

```
{
    "current_password": "correct horse",
    "password": "correct horse battery"
}
```

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Password updated successfully"
    }
}
```

## List Users

This path returns the users, oldest first.

| Method | Path |
| --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/users` |

### Query Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page` | query | int | `1` | `>= 1` | 1-based page index. |
| `per_page` | query | int | `25` | `1…100` | Number of items per page. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "email": "admin@example.com",
                "role_id": 1,
                "password_set": true,
                "oidc_linked": false
            },
            {
                "email": "noc@example.com",
                "role_id": 3,
                "password_set": true,
                "oidc_linked": false
            },
            {
                "email": "viewer@example.com",
                "role_id": 2,
                "password_set": true,
                "oidc_linked": false
            }
        ],
        "page": 1,
        "per_page": 25,
        "total_count": 3
    }
}
```

## Create a User

At most 50 users.

| Method | Path |
| --- | --- |
| POST | `/api/v1/users` |

### Request Body

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `email` | string | Yes | Email address. ASCII letters are stored in lower case. |
| `password` | string | No | Empty, or 8 to 72 bytes. Empty or without it, the user logs in only through the [identity provider](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/reference/api/oidc/index.md>). |
| `role_id` | int | Yes | `1` to `3`. See [roles](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/reference/api/index.md#roles>). |

### Sample Request

```
{
    "email": "noc@example.com",
    "password": "another horse",
    "role_id": 3
}
```

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "User created successfully"
    }
}
```

## Get a User

The email matches in any case.

| Method | Path |
| --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/users/{email}` |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "email": "noc@example.com",
        "role_id": 3,
        "password_set": true,
        "oidc_linked": false
    }
}
```

## Update a User

This path sets the role of a user. A role change ends the user's sessions. An Admin cannot change its own role, and the last Admin with a password stays an Admin. A role from [group roles](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/reference/api/oidc/index.md#group-roles>) cannot be changed.

| Method | Path |
| --- | --- |
| PUT | `/api/v1/users/{email}` |

### Request Body

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `role_id` | int | Yes | `1` to `3`. |

### Sample Request

```
{
    "role_id": 2
}
```

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "User updated successfully"
    }
}
```

## Update a User's Password

This path ends the user's sessions. An Admin cannot update its own password here.

| Method | Path |
| --- | --- |
| PUT | `/api/v1/users/{email}/password` |

### Request Body

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `password` | string | Yes | 8 to 72 bytes. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Password updated successfully"
    }
}
```

## Remove a User's Password

This path removes the password of a user, who can then log in only through the [identity provider](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/reference/api/oidc/index.md>). It ends the user's sessions. An Admin cannot remove its own password, and the last Admin with a password keeps it.

| Method | Path |
| --- | --- |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/users/{email}/password` |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Password removed successfully"
    }
}
```

## Unlink a User

This path unlinks a user from their account at the identity provider, and ends the sessions started through it. An Admin cannot unlink itself.

| Method | Path |
| --- | --- |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/users/{email}/oidc` |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "User unlinked successfully"
    }
}
```

## Delete a User

This path deletes the user with its sessions and API tokens. An Admin cannot delete itself, and the last Admin with a password cannot be deleted.

| Method | Path |
| --- | --- |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/users/{email}` |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "User deleted successfully"
    }
}
```

## Create an API Token

This path returns the token, the only time it is shown. At most 12 per user. Requires an access token.

| Method | Path |
| --- | --- |
| POST | `/api/v1/users/me/api-tokens` |
| POST | `/api/v1/users/{email}/api-tokens` |

### Request Body

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | Yes | 3 to 50 characters, unique among the user's tokens. |
| `expires_at` | string | No | RFC 3339 time in the future. Without it, the token does not expire. |

### Response Fields

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `token` | string | `ellamocn_`, the token identifier, `_` and the secret. |

### Sample Request

```
{
    "name": "Prometheus scraper",
    "expires_at": "2027-11-13T00:00:00Z"
}
```

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "token": "ellamocn_95Q0Y4lBtx2O_FAPT4VAIG3XDCT2V3D2LTEEYCS"
    }
}
```

## List API Tokens

This path returns the user's API tokens, oldest first.

| Method | Path |
| --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/users/me/api-tokens` |
| GET | `/api/v1/users/{email}/api-tokens` |

### Query Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page` | query | int | `1` | `>= 1` | 1-based page index. |
| `per_page` | query | int | `25` | `1…100` | Number of items per page. |

### Response Fields

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | Token identifier: the part of the token between `ellamocn_` and the next `_`. |
| `name` | string | Name. |
| `created_at` | string | Creation time. |
| `expires_at` | string | Expiry time. Absent for a token that does not expire. |
| `last_used_at` | string | Time of the last use, updated at most once a minute. Absent for a token never used. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "id": "95Q0Y4lBtx2O",
                "name": "Prometheus scraper",
                "created_at": "2026-11-13T16:30:39.168Z",
                "expires_at": "2027-11-13T00:00:00.000Z",
                "last_used_at": "2026-11-13T16:30:55.267Z"
            }
        ],
        "page": 1,
        "per_page": 25,
        "total_count": 1
    }
}
```

## Delete an API Token

| Method | Path |
| --- | --- |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/users/me/api-tokens/{id}` |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/users/{email}/api-tokens/{id}` |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "API token deleted successfully"
    }
}
```

# Configuration File

Ella MOCN is configured using a YAML file. Start Ella MOCN with the `--config` flag to specify its path. Unknown keys are rejected. Changes take effect on restart.

The operators and radios are not in this file: they are in the database, and set with the UI or the [API](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/reference/api/index.md>).

## Parameters

- `logging` (object, optional): The logging configuration.

  - `level` (string, optional): The log level: `debug`, `info`, `warn`, or `error`. Default `info`.
- `db` (object): The database configuration.

  - `path` (string): The path to the SQLite database file.
- `api` (object, optional): The HTTP API and UI.

  - `address` (string, optional): The IP address to listen on. Default `0.0.0.0`.
  - `port` (int, optional): The TCP port to listen on. Default `5030`.
  - `tls` (object, optional): Serve over HTTPS, TLS 1.2 or later. Default: plain HTTP.

    - `cert` (string): The path to the PEM certificate chain, the server's certificate first.
    - `key` (string): The path to the PEM private key.
- `ran` (object, optional): The radios.

  - `signalling` (object, optional): The S1 and NG listeners that radios connect to.

    - `address` (string, optional): The IP address to listen on. Default `0.0.0.0`.
    - `s1_port` (int, optional): The SCTP port of S1. Default `36412`.
    - `ng_port` (int, optional): The SCTP port of NG. Default `38412`.
  - `user_plane` (object, optional): The user plane towards the radios.

    - `enabled` (boolean, optional): Allow [user-plane aggregation](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/explanation/user_plane_aggregation_with_ebpf/index.md>). When `true`, Ella MOCN sets `net.ipv4.ip_forward` and `net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding` to `1` at startup and needs the capabilities in the [system requirements](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/reference/system_reqs/index.md>). When `false`, every operator uses the direct user plane. Default `false`.
    - `name` (string): The network interface that radios' user traffic arrives on. Ella MOCN's address is its first global IPv4 address, or else its first global IPv6 address. Either `name` or `address` must be set when `enabled` is `true`, not both.
    - `address` (string): Ella MOCN's user-plane address towards the radios. A unicast address of an interface of the host. Either `name` or `address` must be set when `enabled` is `true`, not both.
- `telemetry` (object, optional): The [traces](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/reference/observability/index.md#traces>).

  - `enabled` (boolean, optional): Export traces. Default `false`.
  - `otlp_endpoint` (string): The `host:port` of an OTLP/gRPC collector, over plain gRPC. Required when `enabled` is `true`.

With the snap, the configuration file is `/var/snap/ella-mocn/common/mocn.yaml`.

## Example

```
logging:
  level: info
db:
  path: /var/lib/mocn/mocn.db
api:
  address: 0.0.0.0
  port: 5030
  tls:
    cert: /etc/mocn/api.pem
    key: /etc/mocn/api.key
ran:
  signalling:
    address: 0.0.0.0
    s1_port: 36412
    ng_port: 38412
  user_plane:
    enabled: true
    name: eth1
telemetry:
  enabled: true
  otlp_endpoint: localhost:4317
```

# Connectivity

The interfaces Ella MOCN exposes and the peers it connects to. Defaults are in parentheses.

| Interface | Peer | Transport | Local address | Remote address | Port | Used |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| API and UI | Users, applications, Prometheus | TCP, or TLS with `api.tls` | `api.address` (`0.0.0.0`) |  | `api.port` (`5030`) | Always |
| S1, from radios | eNBs | SCTP, PPID `18` | `ran.signalling.address` (`0.0.0.0`) |  | `ran.signalling.s1_port` (`36412`) | Always |
| NG, from radios | gNBs | SCTP, PPID `60` | `ran.signalling.address` (`0.0.0.0`) |  | `ran.signalling.ng_port` (`38412`) | Always |
| S1, to MMEs | The operators' MMEs | SCTP, PPID `18` | Source address of the host's route to the MME (`src`) | The MME's `tnl_addresses` | `36412` | Always |
| NG, to AMFs | The operators' AMFs | SCTP, PPID `60` | Source address of the host's route to the AMF (`src`) | The AMF's `tnl_addresses` | `38412` | Always |
| GTP-U, with radios | eNBs, gNBs | GTP-U over UDP | `ran.user_plane.address`, or the address of `ran.user_plane.name` |  | `2152` | Only with `ran.user_plane.enabled`, for operators with user-plane aggregation |
| GTP-U, with operators | The operators' S-GWs and UPFs | GTP-U over UDP | Same as S1 or NG to the operator; for the other IP version, source address of the host's route to the S-GW or UPF |  | `2152` | Only with `ran.user_plane.enabled`, for operators with user-plane aggregation |
| OTLP | OpenTelemetry collector | gRPC over TCP, without TLS |  | `telemetry.otlp_endpoint` | `telemetry.otlp_endpoint` | Only with `telemetry.enabled` |

# Observability

Ella MOCN supports four observability pillars: Logs, Metrics, Traces and Profiles.

## Logs

Ella MOCN writes its logs to standard output, one JSON object per line, at the level of `logging.level` in the [configuration file](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/reference/config_file/index.md>): `debug`, `info`, `warn` or `error`.

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `ts` | Time of the event. |
| `level` | `debug`, `info`, `warn` or `error`. |
| `msg` | What happened. |
| `trace_id` | Trace ID of the span the event happened in, as 32 hex digits. Absent outside a span. |
| `span_id` | Span ID of the span the event happened in, as 16 hex digits. Absent outside a span. |
| `trace_flags` | W3C trace flags of that span, as 2 hex digits: `01` when sampled. Absent outside a span. |

Other fields depend on the event.

### Audit events

Audit events are logs at level `info` with `msg` set to `audit event`.

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `action` | What was done, such as `auth_login`, `auth_oidc_login` or `create_operator`. |
| `actor` | Email of the user who did it. Empty when unknown. |
| `ip` | Address the request came from. |
| `details` | What was done, in words. |

## Metrics

Ella MOCN exposes Prometheus metrics at [`GET /api/v1/metrics`](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/reference/api/metrics/index.md>).

| Metric | Type | Labels | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ellamocn_radio_associations` | Gauge | `interface`, `state` (`connected`, `up`, `setup_failed`) | Radios connected, by state: `connected` before the S1 or NG Setup, `up` after, `setup_failed` after Ella MOCN rejected the last S1 or NG Setup. |
| `ellamocn_core_associations` | Gauge | `interface`, `operator`, `state` (`disconnected`, `connected`, `up`, `setup_failed`) | Associations to MMEs and AMFs, by operator and state. |
| `ellamocn_core_overloaded` | Gauge | `interface`, `operator` | MMEs and AMFs reporting overload, by operator. |
| `ellamocn_setup_attempts_total` | Counter | `interface`, `side` (`radio`, `core`), `result` (`success`, `failure`, `timeout`, `unknown_plmn`, …) | S1 and NG Setup attempts from radios (`radio`) and to MMEs and AMFs (`core`), by result. |
| `ellamocn_initial_ue_messages_total` | Counter | `interface`, `result` (`relayed`, `unknown_plmn`, `no_mme`, `no_amf`, `rejected`, `invalid`, `error`) | New UE connections from radios, by result. |
| `ellamocn_paging_messages_total` | Counter | `interface`, `result` (`relayed`, `no_radio`, `invalid`) | Paging messages from MMEs and AMFs, by result. |
| `ellamocn_overload_messages_total` | Counter | `interface`, `procedure` (`overload_start`, `overload_stop`), `result` (`relayed`, `no_radio`, `ignored`, `invalid`) | Overload start and stop messages from MMEs and AMFs, by result. |
| `ellamocn_handover_messages_total` | Counter | `interface`, `procedure` (`handover_request`, `path_switch_request`), `result` (`relayed`, `no_radio`, `no_mme`, `no_amf`, `invalid`, `error`) | Handover and path switch requests, by result. |
| `ellamocn_pws_messages_total` | Counter | `interface`, `procedure` (`write_replace_warning`, `kill`, `pws_cancel`, `pws_restart_indication`, `pws_failure_indication`), `result` (`relayed`, `no_radio`, `timeout`, …) | Public warning requests from MMEs and AMFs and indications from radios, by result. |
| `ellamocn_ue_connections` | Gauge | `interface`, `operator` | UE connections relayed, by operator. |
| `ellamocn_api_request_duration_seconds` | Histogram | `method`, `route`, `code` | Duration of API requests. |
| `ellamocn_oidc_logins_total` | Counter | `outcome` (`success`, or a [login error](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/reference/api/auth/index.md#errors>)) | Logins through the identity provider, by outcome. |
| `ellamocn_database_query_duration_seconds` | Histogram | `pool` (`write`, `read`) | Duration of database queries. |
| `ellamocn_database_query_errors_total` | Counter | `pool` (`write`, `read`) | Failed database queries. |
| `ellamocn_database_storage_bytes` | Gauge | `file` (`main`, `wal`) | Size of the database on disk. |
| `ellamocn_build_info` | Gauge | `version`, `revision`, `branch`, `goversion`, `goos`, `goarch`, `tags` | Build information. Always 1. |
| `go_*` | Gauge, Counter, Summary |  | Go runtime. |
| `process_*` | Gauge, Counter |  | Process memory, CPU and file descriptors. |

### User-plane metrics

With [user-plane aggregation](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/explanation/user_plane_aggregation_with_ebpf/index.md>):

| Metric | Type | Labels | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ellamocn_user_plane_enabled` | Gauge |  | 1 when `ran.user_plane.enabled` is `true` in the [configuration file](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/reference/config_file/index.md>), 0 otherwise. |
| `ellamocn_user_plane_datapath_loaded` | Gauge |  | 1 while the user-plane eBPF program is loaded, 0 otherwise. |
| `ellamocn_user_plane_state` | Gauge | `operator`, `state` (`ready`, `unavailable`, `off`) | 1 for the operator's current [user-plane state](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/reference/api/operators/index.md>), 0 for the other states. |
| `ellamocn_user_plane_unavailable` | Gauge | `operator`, `reason` (`not_connected`, `no_route`, `route_mismatch`, `no_address`, `interface_error`, `too_many_operators`) | 1 for the [reason](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/reference/api/operators/index.md>) while the state is `unavailable`, 0 otherwise. |
| `ellamocn_user_plane_tunnels` | Gauge | `operator`, `direction` | GTP-U tunnels relayed. |
| `ellamocn_user_plane_tunnel_setups_total` | Counter | `operator`, `direction` | GTP-U tunnels set up. |
| `ellamocn_user_plane_tunnel_setup_failures_total` | Counter | `operator`, `interface` (`s1`, `ng`), `procedure`, `reason` (`user_plane_unavailable`, `no_route`, `route_mismatch`, `no_address`, `no_teid`, `too_many_paths`, `invalid_address`, `unknown_endpoint`, `other`) | Procedures whose user-plane transport could not be relayed. The UE is released, or the handover or path switch is rejected. |
| `ellamocn_user_plane_packets_total` | Counter | `operator`, `radio`, `direction` | G-PDUs relayed. End Marker and Tunnel Status messages are not counted. |
| `ellamocn_user_plane_bytes_total` | Counter | `operator`, `radio`, `direction` | Octets of the T-PDUs of the G-PDUs relayed: the inner IP packet, without the GTP-U header and extension headers. |
| `ellamocn_user_plane_dropped_packets_total` | Counter | `operator`, `path` (`fast`, `slow`), `reason` | GTP-U messages dropped. |
| `ellamocn_user_plane_slow_path_packets_total` | Counter | `reason` | Packets on user-plane interfaces that the fast path left to the kernel. |
| `ellamocn_user_plane_slow_path_relayed_total` | Counter | `operator`, `direction` | G-PDUs, End Markers and Tunnel Status messages relayed by the slow path. |
| `ellamocn_user_plane_error_indications_total` | Counter | `origin`, `result` | GTP-U Error Indications. |
| `ellamocn_user_plane_peer_up` | Gauge | `operator`, `side` (`radio`, `core`), `peer` | 0 once 3 Echo Requests in a row, sent every 60 s, go unanswered, 3 to 4 minutes after the peer stops answering. 1 otherwise. Present while a tunnel of the operator relays to the peer. |
| `ellamocn_user_plane_bpf_map_entries` | Gauge | `map` (`tunnels`, `tunnel_stats`, `ifaces`, `path_stats`) | Entries in a map of the user-plane datapath. |
| `ellamocn_user_plane_bpf_map_max_entries` | Gauge | `map` (`tunnels`, `tunnel_stats`, `ifaces`, `path_stats`) | Capacity of a map of the user-plane datapath. |
| `ellamocn_user_plane_bpf_map_memory_bytes` | Gauge | `map` (`tunnels`, `tunnel_stats`, `ifaces`, `config`, `path_stats`, `drops`, `passes`) | Kernel memory locked by a map of the user-plane datapath. |

## Traces

Ella MOCN exports [OpenTelemetry](<https://opentelemetry.io/>) traces when `telemetry.enabled` is set in the [configuration file](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/reference/config_file/index.md>).

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Export | OTLP over gRPC, without TLS |
| Service | `ella-mocn` |
| Sampling | Parent-based, always on for a trace the MOCN starts |
| Propagation | W3C Trace Context |
| S1AP, NGAP and database spans | No NAS, security keys, subscriber identity, SQL text or parameters |

### Spans

| Span | Kind | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{method} {route}` | Server | A request to the API, except `/api/v1/livez`, `/api/v1/readyz`, `/api/v1/metrics` and `/api/v1/pprof/`. Links to the caller's `traceparent`. |
| `s1ap/receive` | Server, Consumer | An S1AP message from a radio or an MME. |
| `s1ap/send` | Client, Producer | An S1AP message to a radio or an MME, a child of the `s1ap/receive` that caused it. |
| `ngap/receive` | Server, Consumer | An NGAP message from a radio or an AMF. |
| `ngap/send` | Client, Producer | An NGAP message to a radio or an AMF, a child of the `ngap/receive` that caused it. |
| `db.{call}`, such as `db.CreateUser` | Internal | A database call within a trace. |

### RAN trace correlation

When an MME or AMF activates a trace for a UE, that UE's S1AP or NGAP spans join the core's trace.

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| OpenTelemetry trace ID | 8 octets `0x00` ‖ E-UTRAN Trace ID or NG-RAN Trace ID (8 octets) |

## Profiles

Ella MOCN exposes the [net/http/pprof](<https://pkg.go.dev/net/http/pprof>) API at [`/api/v1/pprof/`](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/reference/api/pprof/index.md>).

## Dashboards

Ella MOCN ships with a [Grafana](<https://grafana.com/>) dashboard. Import its JSON file from the repository.

### Overview

This dashboard uses Prometheus metrics to show the health of Ella MOCN on one screen: service status, radios and UE connections by operator, and performance.

[![Overview Dashboard](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/images/dashboard_overview.png>)](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/images/dashboard_overview.png>)

Grafana dashboard for Overview.

- Data Sources: Prometheus
- Dashboard JSON: [observability/grafana/dashboards/overview.json](<https://github.com/ellanetworks/mocn/blob/main/observability/grafana/dashboards/overview.json>)

To import it, open **Dashboards \> New \> Import** in Grafana and upload the JSON file.

# Performance

This reference document contains performance test results of Ella MOCN's datapath with [user-plane aggregation](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/explanation/user_plane_aggregation_with_ebpf/index.md>), and of its signalling.

On a 16-vCPU virtual machine, Ella MOCN forwards 15 Gbps of subscriber traffic at 0% loss using about 3 vCPUs, adds under 0.1 ms of round-trip latency, and uses about 480 MiB of memory with 100,000 sessions. On a 20-core host, it relays 17,000 4G attaches or 11,000 5G registrations per second with user-plane aggregation.

## Datapath

### Throughput

The following table outlines Ella MOCN's user-plane throughput at 0% loss, in millions of packets per second (Mpps) and gigabits per second (Gbps), for subscriber IP packets of 46, 494 and 1456 bytes:

Table 1. User-plane throughput at 0% loss

<table> <thead>     <tr>       <th rowspan="2">Network</th>       <th rowspan="2">Direction</th>       <th colspan="3">Throughput (Mpps)</th>       <th colspan="3">Throughput (Gbps)</th>     </tr>     <tr>       <th>46 B</th>       <th>494 B</th>       <th>1456 B</th>       <th>46 B</th>       <th>494 B</th>       <th>1456 B</th>     </tr>   </thead> <tbody>     <tr><td rowspan="2">4G</td><td>Uplink</td><td>1.95</td><td>1.87</td><td>1.29</td><td>0.72</td><td>7.41</td><td>15.0</td></tr>     <tr><td>Downlink</td><td>1.64</td><td>1.92</td><td>1.38</td><td>0.60</td><td>7.60</td><td>16.1</td></tr>   </tbody> <tbody>     <tr><td rowspan="2">5G</td><td>Uplink</td><td>1.76</td><td>1.36</td><td>1.20</td><td>0.65</td><td>5.37</td><td>14.0</td></tr>     <tr><td>Downlink</td><td>1.85</td><td>1.38</td><td>1.32</td><td>0.68</td><td>5.46</td><td>15.3</td></tr>   </tbody> </table>

The packet size represents only the IP packet for the subscribers and ignores Ethernet and GTP-U encapsulation.

All packets through Ella MOCN were relayed by the eBPF fast path: `ellamocn_user_plane_slow_path_packets_total` and `ellamocn_user_plane_dropped_packets_total` stayed at 0.

### Latency (Round-trip)

The following table outlines the user-plane round-trip latency:

Table 2. User-plane round-trip latency

| Path | Average (ms) | Best (ms) | Worst (ms) | Mean Deviation (ms) | p99 (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Through Ella MOCN | 0.264 | 0.204 | 1.135 | 0.028 | 0.432 |
| Direct | 0.179 | 0.114 | 0.637 | 0.022 | 0.276 |

The value represents the round-trip time from a radio to the operator's S-GW and back.

### CPU

The following table outlines the CPU used on the Ella MOCN host at the throughput above, in vCPUs:

Table 3. CPU on the Ella MOCN host (vCPUs)

| Direction | 46 B | 494 B | 1456 B |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Uplink | 2.8 | 2.9 | 2.6 |
| Downlink | 2.3 | 3.0 | 2.7 |

No vCPU exceeded 77%.

### Memory

The following table outlines the memory of the user plane by number of sessions, with one E-RAB and two GTP-U tunnels per session, on a host with 16 vCPUs:

Table 4. User-plane memory

| Sessions | Tunnels | eBPF maps (MiB) | Ella MOCN process RSS (MiB) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 0 | 36.3 | 42.8 |
| 10,000 | 20,000 | 40.7 | 101.6 |
| 100,000 | 200,000 | 80.5 | 399.2 |

Table 5. eBPF map memory

| eBPF map | Fixed | Per tunnel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tunnels` | 16.0 MiB | 136 B |
| `tunnel_stats` | 16.0 MiB | 96 B |
| `path_stats` | 264 KiB per CPU |  |
| Others | 143 KiB |  |

eBPF map memory is kernel memory and is not part of the process RSS.

### Methodology

We performed performance tests with Ella MOCN on Google Cloud, with three virtual machines in the same zone, of the following specifications:

- **Machine type**: n2-standard-16 (16 vCPUs, 64 GB RAM)
- **OS**: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, kernel 7.0.0-1017-gcp
- **NICs**: 2 x gVNIC, 4 receive and 4 transmit queues each, MTU 1500
- **Networks**: one for the radios and one for the operator

The Ella MOCN host had `ran.user_plane.enabled` set to `true`, the `forward` chain policy of nftables set to drop, its NIC interrupts spread over all vCPUs, and the `nohz=off` kernel parameter.

The tests used `mocnperf`, in the `perf/` directory of the Ella MOCN repository: fake eNBs and a fake MME (4G), or fake gNBs and a fake AMF (5G), set up the sessions through Ella MOCN, a generator sent GTP-U from `AF_PACKET` sockets, and an XDP program counted the packets received.

Test parameters:

- **Sessions**: 1024, one E-RAB each
- **Radios**: 64, each at its own address
- **S-GWs**: 16 addresses
- **Search**: highest rate at 0% loss (RFC 2544), binary search with 5-second trials and 2% resolution
- **Confirmation**: 10 seconds at 0% loss
- **Runs**: 1

Latency test parameters:

- **Probes**: 1000 per round, one every 10 ms
- **Rounds**: 5 through Ella MOCN and 5 direct, alternating, median
- **Packet size**: 84 B

## Signalling

### Procedure Rate and Latency

The following table outlines the highest rate of procedures Ella MOCN relayed, with 160 procedures in flight, and the time each took:

Table 6. Signalling procedure rate and latency

| Procedure | User-plane aggregation | Rate (/s) | p50 (ms) | p99 (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4G attach | Off | 43,981 | 2.27 | 3.74 |
| 4G attach | On | 17,102 | 6.18 | 9.23 |
| 5G registration | Off | 28,214 | 2.20 | 3.64 |
| 5G registration | On | 11,763 | 4.06 | 8.63 |
| 5G PDU session establishment | Off | 28,214 | 2.05 | 3.47 |
| 5G PDU session establishment | On | 11,763 | 6.72 | 10.97 |
| 4G paging |  | 87,961 | 1.76 | 3.77 |
| 5G paging |  | 103,679 | 1.55 | 3.15 |

The time of a 4G attach or 5G registration runs from the radio's Initial UE Message to the core's Initial Context Setup Request. The time of a PDU session establishment runs from the gNB's Uplink NAS Transport to the AMF's PDU Session Resource Setup Request. The time of a paging runs from the core's Paging to its arrival at every radio in the paging area. In 5G, each UE registers, then establishes one PDU session.

### Memory

The following table outlines the memory of 100,000 connected UEs, with user-plane aggregation:

Table 7. Signalling memory with 100,000 connected UEs

| Procedure | Connection rate (/s) | Memory per UE |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4G attach | 20,783 | 4.7 KB |
| 5G registration and PDU session establishment | 12,463 | 5.2 KB |

Memory per UE is the process RSS growth from 0 to 100,000 connected UEs, divided by 100,000, and includes the simulated radios and cores. eBPF map memory is in the [datapath memory](<#memory>).

### Methodology

We performed signalling tests on one host, with the following specifications:

- **CPU**: Intel Core Ultra 7 265K, 20 cores
- **Memory**: 64 GB
- **OS**: Ubuntu, kernel 7.0.0

The tests used the end-to-end benchmarks in `internal/e2ebench` of the Ella MOCN repository: Ella MOCN, simulated eNBs or gNBs, and simulated MMEs or AMFs of two operators ran in one process on the host, over SCTP. Each UE was released after its procedure.

Test parameters:

- **Procedures in flight**: 160, one radio per procedure
- **Paging area**: 8 radios
- **Duration**: 5 seconds per run
- **Runs**: 3, median
- **Memory test**: 100,000 UEs on 100 radios, 256 procedures in flight

# System Requirements

Ella MOCN runs on any Linux distribution, on amd64 and arm64.

|  | Up to 10,000 subscribers | Up to 100,000 subscribers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Operating System** | Linux, kernel 6.6 or later with SCTP | Linux, kernel 6.6 or later with SCTP |
| **CPU** | 2 cores, amd64 or arm64 | 4 cores, amd64 or arm64 |
| **Memory** | 1 GB RAM | 2 GB RAM |
| **Disk** | 10 GB | 10 GB |
| **Capabilities** | `CAP_BPF`, `CAP_PERFMON`, `CAP_NET_ADMIN` and `CAP_NET_RAW` (if user-plane aggregation is enabled) | `CAP_BPF`, `CAP_PERFMON`, `CAP_NET_ADMIN` and `CAP_NET_RAW` (if user-plane aggregation is enabled) |

## Kubernetes

Ella MOCN should work on most Kubernetes distributions. It has been validated on **GKE**, **OpenShift**, **RKE2**, and **kind**.

| Requirement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Nodes** | Meet the host requirements above |
| **Kubernetes** | 1.30 or later, with SCTP Services |
| **RAN network** | Radios reach Ella MOCN's S1 and NG ports, either through an SCTP `LoadBalancer` or `NodePort` Service, or at the pod's address on a [Multus](<https://github.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/multus-cni>) network. On a Multus network, the Helm chart uses the `macvlan` and `static` [CNI plugins](<https://github.com/containernetworking/plugins>). |
| **User-plane aggregation** | A Multus network, with the `tuning` CNI plugin allowed to set `net.ipv4.ip_forward` and `net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding` |
| **Pod Security** | `restricted`, or `privileged` with user-plane aggregation or IPsec |
| **Capabilities** | None, or `BPF`, `PERFMON`, `NET_ADMIN` and `NET_RAW` with user-plane aggregation |
| **IPsec** | `NET_ADMIN` and `NET_BIND_SERVICE` for the strongSwan sidecar; amd64 nodes |
| **Storage** | A default StorageClass with `ReadWriteOnce` volumes |

# Explanation

# Architecture

Ella MOCN is a Multi-Operator Core Network (MOCN) gateway. It lets one neutral host radio network serve the subscribers of several mobile operators, with each operator keeping its own core network.

[![Neutral host architecture](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/images/architecture.svg>)](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/images/architecture.svg>)

Neutral host architecture

## What each side sees

- **Radios** connect to Ella MOCN as if it were their core. They broadcast the networks of every operator they serve, and need no per-operator configuration.
- **Each operator** sees Ella MOCN as a single base station. The operator provisions one node, however large the neutral host's network grows.

Adding an operator does not touch the radios, and adding a radio does not involve the operators.

When a phone connects, it picks one of the networks the radio broadcasts, and Ella MOCN sends its signalling to the operator that owns that network.

## Mobility

When a phone moves between radios, the operator's core stays in charge of the handover, as it would with its own radios. Ella MOCN delivers the handover to the right radio, so phones keep their connection as they move through the neutral host's network. The core finds Ella MOCN by tracking area, so the neutral host's tracking areas must not be reused elsewhere in the operator's network.

## Public warnings

The sharing operators agree on one of them to send public warnings, such as emergency alerts, for the whole shared network. Ella MOCN broadcasts that operator's warnings on every radio in the warning area, and does not broadcast warnings from the others. When a radio restarts, Ella MOCN tells that operator, so its warnings are sent to the radio again.

# Explanation

These pages explain how Ella MOCN works and why.

- [Architecture](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/explanation/architecture/index.md>)
- [User-Plane Aggregation with eBPF](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/explanation/user_plane_aggregation_with_ebpf/index.md>)
- [Security](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/explanation/security/index.md>)
- [Single Sign-On](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/explanation/single_sign_on/index.md>)

# Security

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Info**
>
> To report a security vulnerability, please file a [Private Security Report](<https://github.com/ellanetworks/mocn/security/advisories/new>).

Security is one of Ella MOCN's core tenets. From the UI to the database, security is built into every layer of the system.

## Authentication & Authorization

Ella MOCN enforces authentication on API requests towards most endpoints. Two authentication methods are supported:

- **Session-based authentication.** Users authenticate with email and password, or through [single sign-on](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/explanation/single_sign_on/index.md>). A session cookie and a short-lived access token are issued. The login endpoint limits attempts per client address and per account.
- **API tokens.** Per-user tokens that can expire and be revoked individually. A token has its user's role, but cannot create API tokens, change a password or manage users. Recommended for programmatic access.

### Role-Based Access Control

Every request is authorized against a role-based permission system with three built-in roles:

| Role | Scope |
| --- | --- |
| **Admin** | Full access to all resources and operations. |
| **Network Manager** | Read Only, plus creating, updating and deleting operators. Cannot manage users. |
| **Read Only** | Reads operators, radios and UE connections. |

## Secret Storage

- **User passwords** are stored as one-way hashes. Verification uses constant-time comparison.
- **API token secrets** are stored as one-way hashes. The raw token is returned only once at creation time and is never retrievable afterward.
- **Session tokens** are cryptographically random values. Only a one-way hash is persisted.
- **JWT signing secret** is a cryptographically random value generated once and stored in the database.

## Transport Security

### API and UI

Ella MOCN uses TLS to secure its API and web interface. The TLS configuration is defined in the [configuration file](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/reference/config_file/index.md>).

Ella MOCN supports TLS `1.2` and `1.3`.

### Operators

Ella MOCN can reach operator cores with IPsec tunnels. The tunnels are set up on the host, and Ella MOCN uses them to reach the operator's MMEs and AMFs, and its S-GWs and UPFs with [user-plane aggregation](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/explanation/user_plane_aggregation_with_ebpf/index.md>). See [Connect an Operator over IPsec](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/how_to/connect_an_operator_over_ipsec/index.md>).

### Radios

Ella MOCN does not encrypt S1 and NG toward the radios, and does not check a radio's identity. Protect the link to the radios, for example with IPsec set up on the host or a private network.

## Minimal Attack Surface

Ella MOCN minimizes its attack surface through minimal packaging:

- **Container image.** Built on a distroless base with no operating system layer, shell, or package manager. Only the strictly necessary runtime dependencies are included. Image size: **under 100 MB**.

## Audit Logging

Ella MOCN writes security-relevant events, such as logins and changes to operators and users, to its log as audit events. Each records who did what, and when.

# Single Sign-On

Users can log in to the UI through the organization's identity provider instead of, or as well as, a password. Ella MOCN works with any OpenID Connect identity provider, such as Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, Ping Identity, Google or Keycloak. To set it up, see [Configure Single Sign-On](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/how_to/configure_single_sign_on/index.md>).

[![Login page with single sign-on](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/images/sso_login.png>)](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/images/sso_login.png>)

Login page with single sign-on

## Password and single sign-on

|  | Password | Single sign-on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Credentials kept by | Ella MOCN | The identity provider, with its own policies, such as multi-factor authentication |
| Role set by | An Admin | An Admin, or the highest role from the user's groups at the identity provider |
| Session | 30 days | The session lifetime, 24 hours by default |
| Access removed by | Deleting the user in Ella MOCN, at once | Removing the user at the identity provider, at the end of their session |

Password login stays when single sign-on is on, and at least one Admin always keeps a password. An identity provider that is down or misconfigured cannot lock everyone out.

## Matching users

A user is matched to their account at the identity provider, not to their email address, so a changed or reused email address does not give access to another user. The email address is used once, to link the account at its first login, only if the identity provider has verified it and the user has no password. A user with a password links from their profile. A provider that does not say whether email addresses are verified, such as Microsoft Entra ID, must be trusted explicitly: anyone who can set their email address there could take over the matching user. An account with no user in Ella MOCN gets one only from a [group mapping](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/how_to/manage_single_sign_on_users/index.md#map-groups-to-roles>), within the limit of 50 users.

## Offboarding

Ella MOCN does not learn when someone is removed at the identity provider. Their session lasts until its lifetime ends, and their API tokens until deleted. A shorter session lifetime narrows that window, at the cost of logging in more often. To end access at once, [offboard the user](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/how_to/manage_single_sign_on_users/index.md#offboard-a-user>) in Ella MOCN.

# User-Plane Aggregation with eBPF

While signalling always goes through Ella MOCN, you can choose to have subscriber traffic go through Ella MOCN too. This is called user-plane aggregation.

## Direct vs aggregated

[![User-plane aggregation](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/images/user_plane_aggregation.svg>)](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/images/user_plane_aggregation.svg>)

User-plane aggregation

### Direct

Each radio sends its traffic straight to the operator's network. The radios and the operator's network must reach each other, so every radio needs an address the operator can route to.

### Aggregated

Ella MOCN carries the traffic between the radios and the operator's network. The operator sees only Ella MOCN's address, and the radios stay on the neutral host's private network. Subscriber traffic follows the same path as Ella MOCN's signalling to that operator, typically its IPsec tunnel. All of that operator's traffic then depends on Ella MOCN's capacity and availability.

## How Ella MOCN forwards traffic

Ella MOCN uses eBPF to relay subscriber traffic between the radios and the operators' networks in the kernel. With Traffic Control, it puts its own tunnel endpoints in place of the radios' and the operators', so each side only ever sees Ella MOCN. It never touches the traffic inside the tunnels.

## More information

- [How to Enable User-Plane Aggregation](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/how_to/enable_user_plane_aggregation/index.md>).
- [How to Connect an Operator over IPsec](<https://docs.ellanetworks.com/mocn/how_to/connect_an_operator_over_ipsec/index.md>).
